subject: URGENT: Keep-alive drops & retry surge impacting Medius Health streaming
messages:
From: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@mediushealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Medius Platform Ops <platform-ops@mediushealth.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming keep-alive drops causing client timeouts

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in streaming completion failures today around 15:40 PDT. Our client SDK is reporting repeated client-side timeouts and idle disconnects while waiting for responses; subsequently our frontend retries which causes a retry-storm and spikes 429s from your API. We're seeing the following in the Medius logs:
- ~12% 5xx rate for chat completions between 15:40-16:05
- burst of 429s roughly aligned with our retry logic (backoff not kicking in fast enough)
- kids: most fails are idle stream disconnects (no early response from the server)

I attached a pcap and a dashboard screenshot showing the spike. This is affecting our triage flow and clinical workflows — need immediate help.

Can you confirm whether there was any routing/failover activity or regional throttling during that window? We may need an incident call.

Thanks,
Samantha
Platform Reliability
Medius Health
Attachment: medius_stream_logs_0403.pcap (pcap, 2.3MB)
Attachment: 5xx-429-spike-dashboard-20270403.png (png, 480KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@mediushealth.com>
Cc: Medius Platform Ops <platform-ops@mediushealth.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming keep-alive drops causing client timeouts

Samantha — thanks for the fast heads up and the artifacts. I’m escalating internally now and will coordinate a bridge if needed.

Quick asks while we triage: can you confirm the SDK version and whether you observed any client-side disconnects from the browser console? Also: if you can share a sample request-id from the window we’ll pull the server-side traces immediately.

I’m looping in our AE SE and my manager; we’re treating this as P1 given the clinical impact.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: [EXTERNAL] P1: Medius Health — 12% 5xx + retry storm (customer impact)

Team — Samantha from Medius just reported a high-severity production incident: streaming/chat completions are timing out client-side leading to retries and a cascade of 429s. Key facts from the customer artifacts:
- Window: 15:40–16:05 PDT (today)
- Symptom: idle stream disconnects / no data for 15–30s, client times out, then retries
- Observed server-side: ~12% 5xx for the window, 429 surge after retry attempts

Customer impact: clinical triage workflows stalled. They explicitly asked whether anything changed on our routing/region side.

Immediate asks:
1) Rafael / Markus — can we pull per-node streaming logs and the tracing for request-ids in the provided pcap? Look for sudden connection resets or keep-alive timeouts.
2) Sergio — please prepare a short customer-facing summary and propose immediate mitigation (short-term fallback policy: reduce long-poll TTL, bump keep-alive refresh, and suggest client SDK backoff tweaks).
3) Laura — heads up for potential exec escalation; Medius may want credits / SLA mitigation if root cause is on our end.

I confirmed we have a HubSpot ticket HT-7894. I will set up a 30-min bridge if engineering requests it.

Thanks — priority P1.
— Vanessa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] P1: Medius Health — 12% 5xx + retry storm (customer impact)

Vanessa / team — initial triage notes from SE side:
- Pulled logs for the window and correlated with the customer's pcap. We see a pattern of idle connection resets from a subset of proxy workers in us-west-2.
- The worker side shows intermittent kernel-level TCP RSTs and elevated event loop latencies; not all workers affected — roughly 18% of the fleet for that shard.
- No config rollouts were scheduled for that timeframe; autoscaler activity shows a small burst of instance churn but nothing unusual in the config plane.

Immediate mitigation we recommend to limit customer impact:
- Short-term: enable a conservative fallback policy that routes their traffic to a stable model-variant pool (lower concurrency, pin to dedicated nodes) until root cause cleaned. This reduces throughput but stabilizes latencies.
- Also recommend pushing a client-side guidance: increase idle timeout from 20s → 45s and adjust exponential backoff to start at 500ms with jitter to avoid synchronized retries.

I’ll hand off to Markus for ops coordination (re-routing / node pinning).

— Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] P1: Medius Health — 12% 5xx + retry storm (customer impact)

Quick ops update:
- I pinned Medius traffic to a conservative node-pool (variant: v2-small-pin) at 17:02 PDT. Metrics show a drop in 5xx from ~12% → ~2.5% within 6 minutes for pinned traffic. See dashboard snapshot in drive link.
- Enabled per-customer prefix cache and disabled aggressive batching for that customer for the short window. This will increase unit cost but reduces head-of-line stalls.
- We are still investigating the root cause for the kernel-level RSTs on the shard; infra is collecting core dumps and kernel traces.

Customer communication: I prepared a short note (attached draft) proposing the fallback policy and the recommended client SDK backoff adjustments. If legal/procurement demands credits, we should defer until RCA but we can offer a one-time service credit if root cause confirms infra instability.

I’ll keep the bridge open if Medius requests it.
— Markus
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@mediushealth.com>, Medius Platform Ops <platform-ops@mediushealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming keep-alive drops causing client timeouts — short update

Samantha — quick update and immediate steps we took:
- Pinned your traffic to a stable node-pool and enabled prefix caching. You should see a sharp reduction in idle disconnects.
- We recommend you temporarily bump the SDK idle timeout to 45s and add jitter to the retry backoff. We included a short code snippet in the attached draft.
- Our infra team continues to investigate the RSTs; we will provide an RCA within 72 hours.

If you want a 30-min bridge for engineering to walk through the traces, we can do that — we have availability at 11:30 PDT.

We’ll keep monitoring and I’ll follow up with the RCA and any credit guidance once we have internals. Appreciate your patience.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-fallback-policy-draft.docx
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@mediushealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming keep-alive drops causing client timeouts — follow-up and exec note

Vanessa / Laura — thank you for the quick response and the pinning action. We validated that after the pining our errors dropped significantly. Two notes from our CTO:
1) We need the full RCA and timeline for our compliance review next week.
2) If the RCA shows platform instability we will ask for a contractual remediation (credits + SLA change) — please keep sales/legal looped.

Appreciate the responsiveness; will plan for the 11:30 bridge tomorrow if needed.

— Daniel Cho
CTO, Medius Health
